units.translation: 19 lacuna indicated by W, where it seems to have been relegated to v. 230; cf. Ed. Schwartz, De Dion. Scytobr. 1880, 2 n. 2
411-12a. στυφελήν: rough.
b. τετράγυον: Pherecydes in book 6 says it is fifty-yoked (3 fr. 30 J.).
23 l. in P : omitted in L
413a. 〈σπόρον:〉 wheat. Lg
b. ὁλκοῖσι: with the furrows; for as the plow is dragged, the earth is broken up.
c. 〈Δηοῦς:〉 of Demeter. Lg
414. 〈μεταλδήσκοντας:〉 [and] making equal. Lg
28 W separated this gloss from 416b, to which it is attached in L
416a. 〈κείρω:〉 I kill. Lg
b. περισταδόν: standing around in a circle. LgP
3 Apollonius the Sophist, Lexicon Homericum 128, 2 Bekker. Hesychius πάρος. Synagoge π. 333, 28 Bachmann.

427-31a. περιπολλὸν ἐέργεις: The sense: you greatly constrain me with justice, wherefore I, although the contest is superior in force, will undertake it even to death. He used μοῖραν in the masculine gender as μόρον.
6 sch. I 1350 with similar passage
b. ἐέργεις: you constrain, you shut in. LgP
12 sch. I 785 with similar passage
c. οὐ γὰρ ἔτ’ ἄλλο: For nothing is worse for humans than necessity, by which we have come to you, forced by the king. L
438. μετελθεῖν: or μετά instead of πρός; to come to a better man. Lm (P)
10 ἀμείνονα in L : ἀρείονα in P
439. 〈άπηλεγέως:〉 bluntly. Lg

441-42a. τό δὲ ἐπεὶ μεσσηγύς is explanatory of the reason why Argus was walking behind them; because, he says, he nodded to his brothers to remain and stay in the house. And they went and came out, namely those around Jason. P
15 αὑτοῦ Steph. : αὐ-
b. 〈λιπέσθαι:〉 to remain. Lm
444-45a. ἐπ’ αὐτῷ δ’ ὄμματα: And upon him Medea, casting sidelong glances, gazed, holding her veil aside.
b. 〈ἐπ’ αὐτῷ δ’ ὄμματα:〉 the word ἔχουσα is missing. Lg
446-47a. κῆρ ἄχεϊ σμυχ〈οῦσα〉: burning and consuming her soul with grief. L
21 Synagoge σμυχόμενος (367, 24 Bachmann; Photius; Suda)
22 ἀναλ- Hemsterhuis 1743, 372 : ἁλ-
b. νόος δέ οἱ ἠύτ’ ὄνειρος: The sense: with her mind she beheld Jason, as if in a dream she was carried aloft following the footsteps of Jason. L
453. προπρὸ δ’ ἄρ’ ὀφθαλμῶν: the prepositions are emphatic. It indicates her constantly forming images in her mind, as in Homer 'rolling ever forward.' L
455. οἷά τ’ ἔειφ’: he said οἷα in a wondering manner. Lm (P)
460-62. ὀδύρετο δ’ ἠύτε πάμπαν: she lamented him as if already dead, and overcome with pity she wept over him in grief. L
466a. ἐρρέτω: let it perish. L
b. 〈ἡ μὲν ὄφελλεν:〉 or would that she had departed unharmed, having suffered nothing.
4 W separated sch. b from the preceding
